thesis: Author argues that after the earnings drop, the asymmetric upside thesis for FCEL remains intact, emphasizing that decent execution is enough to benefit from AI data center demand, maintaining a bullish stance.
originalText:
Yesterday $FCEL reported their Q3 (fiscal year) earnings and the stock fell ~15%.

Let's objectively review the quarter and see whether our thesis is broken or actually got stronger.

But first I really need to address how X is misrepresenting the thesis that me, @babyfolio and @itsalasdairmann have shared around $FCEL.

Our thesis has NEVER been that $FCEL is better than $BE or that FuelCell Energy is a great operator.

Quite the opposite.

We have repeatedly highlighted that this company has historically been poorly managed, destroyed enormous amounts of shareholder capital through dilution and has a terrible execution history.

That is literally WHY the opportunity is asymmetric.

Simple example:

30% chance of +300%
70% chance of -50%
The most likely outcome is still losing money.

But the expected return is +55%.

THAT is asymmetry. These are not $FCEL specific numbers or my expectations, just want to quickly highlight how X doesn't seem to get that the expected outcome for most asymmetric upside stories is actually the stock going down.

Now back to specifics:

The thesis is that AI data centers suddenly created an enormous need for fast, clean, behind-the-meter power.

Fuel cells are one of the few solutions that fit those requirements, while the clear industry leader $BE appears extremely supply constrained.

$FCEL is therefore entering an unusually favorable demand environment at exactly the moment it is trying to massively expand production.

The market already assumes poor execution.

Our upside case does not require FCEL to suddenly become Bloom.

It requires them to execute DECENTLY.

If they can simultaneously:

1. multiply revenue through higher production
2. improve utilization and margins
3. eventually become profitable

you get the combination of accelerating growth + margin expansion that can drive massive reratings.

Of course execution can fail. We have explicitly called execution the single biggest risk from the beginning.

And importantly: I am genuinely not surprised by this earnings reaction.

Before earnings I literally wrote in my trade alerts:

“I would not be surprised if on earnings we go up or down 20%.”

And when I sold:

“Waiting for a cheap bottom-ish price or confirmation above 50SMA or a fundamental catalyst.”

This is exactly why I sold before the print (and to come off margin in bad macro which I don't feel like is predictable right now).

Now let's look at what the quarter actually told us.

WHAT GOT CONFIRMED:

1) Data center demand is very real for them.

FCEL now has the 30MW firm Fit Energy order, another 350MW of awarded capacity, a NEW 75MW paid capacity reservation with a major data center operator and roughly 10GW of active proposals.

Demand risk for their specific solution clearly went down.

2) Pricing is even better than we modeled.

The Fit agreement implies roughly $3.0M/MW of product value versus the ~$2.75M/MW we previously modeled.

3) Customers are willing to pay upfront to reserve FCEL manufacturing capacity.

This is one of the clearest confirmations of the scarcity thesis.

4) The 500MW expansion remains funded and management continues to target June 2028.

The balance sheet is now extremely strong relative to FCEL's history.

WHAT WAS BAD:

1) Current manufacturing economics are worse than I expected.

At only ~37MW annualized production, FCEL's manufacturing costs are currently ABOVE the contractual pricing of the Fit order.

That is the biggest negative from this quarter.

Our thesis assumes higher utilization will dramatically improve unit economics.

Management believes the same thing.

But they have NOT proven it yet.

-> The main negative to me is not that economics are bad at 37MW utilization. That was expected. It's how slowly they appear to be scaling utilization and moving toward profitable economics. That points back to execution

2) The path to profitability is slower/more uncertain than I previously assumed.

Management now targets positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY2027 and said it likely requires at least 100MW of actual volume, potentially more.

So simply reaching 100MW manufacturing capacity does not automatically mean profitability.

-> Again, not surprising from an economics POV. The genuinely disappointing part is the lack of speed here. The re-rating journey should be beat and raise, but we get underdeliver and overpromise and delay. Again, bad execution.

3) Most of the $2.35B “awarded backlog” is not yet firm backlog.

It is encouraging because FCEL has been selected for the capacity, but those phases still need to convert into definitive contracts.

-> I would give 0 value to anything that isn't a signed contract. Because we already know the demand is there and massive. The bottleneck is capacity anyway.

4) Execution risk increased.

FCEL now has customers and demand.

The question is whether they can manufacture enough product, cheaply enough, quickly enough.

That is exactly what investors should focus on now.

So my conclusion after the quarter is simple:

The DEMAND side of our thesis got completely validated and at this point just seems to be the known facts on the ground.

The EXECUTION side became more questionable. This is the correct attack angle against the thesis.

I do currently think I was too confident about how quickly enormous demand would translate into attractive margins and profitability.

But this is also where the trading discussion matters!

Weak macro + weak chart + a company with huge execution risk going into a binary earnings event is precisely the kind of setup where I personally think active trading can add value.

Some people make fun of selling a stock you remain bullish on long term. I strongly disagree with that way of thinking.

To me, this quarter is a perfect example of why I do it.

I don't need to sit through every execution miss while waiting years for the thesis to play out.

If FCEL starts proving the business inflection, we can still buy it into strength.

If they don't execute, I simply don't have to re-enter.

And because this is still a relatively underfollowed company where most attention goes to the headline revenue, EPS and stock move, I don't think you need to perfectly bottom-tick it.

If FCEL actually starts converting demand, scaling production and showing margin improvement, there should still be years of growth ahead.

The next major proof point is the 100MW production ramp.

If FCEL reaches that level and unit economics improve dramatically, the rerating thesis remains very much alive.

If they ramp production and margins remain terrible, then we have a much bigger fundamental problem.

For now, FCEL appears to have finally found the market it spent decades waiting for.

Now it has to prove it can actually serve it profitably.

As of today, execution is disappointing to me, but not yet thesis-breaking.

We gave them a 2/5 score on exeuction risk (1 = worst, 5 = best).

Personally, I’ll keep following the company and re-enter if they start delivering. If they don’t, I simply won’t re-enter. It’s that simple.

originalText:
𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗢 𝗛𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗜𝗢 𝗥𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧 𝗡𝗢𝗪?

Before you read this on how I recommend hedging your portfolio in the current environment, first read my previous tweet below it: “What Are You Hedging Against?”

The idea is simple. If your kid rides his bike only inside the house, you probably don’t need to insure it against a total loss. That would be expensive and unnecessary. You insure against the kind of damage that is actually likely to happen.

Same with hedging. First define what you are protecting against. Then build the hedge around that risk.

If everyone is already afraid of a 10% correction and hedge funds have already deleveraged, I struggle to see where the sellers come from for a full 10% drawdown.

But let’s assume they are partially right and we get a correction.

I see four possible outcomes over the next 45 days, into the October 16 expiration:

5% chance: market goes up 5% in the next 45 days

30% chance: The market goes higher. You deleveraged, so you barely participate.

30% chance: The market stays around current levels. Some stocks do well, but because you deleveraged, you probably don’t.

30% chance: We follow the historical pattern and the market corrects, but because everyone is already positioned for it, the drawdown is more like 1% to 7%, not 10%.

5% chance: The market actually falls 10% or more.

Taking that distribution into account, I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration:

Buy the 715 put.
Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower.
Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher.
It’s opened for a $19 credit.

The trade does especially well if the market falls somewhere between roughly 5% and 11%.

The idea is simple: stay exposed to some upside while protecting yourself against the kind of downside I think is actually more likely over the next 45 days.

Walking to a restaurant right now so I'm typing as fast as possible… $NBIS is best in class for many reasons… if their strategy was just to keep doing hyperscaler deals I’d be less bullish but I believe they’re one of the few neoclouds (or neoscalers) that has a truly specialized and differentiated offering whereby they will command higher mid-term and short-rates (for longer) which really changes the economics and then the asset light model should be icing on the cake depending on the size and scope of those deals… I assume it will be a rev share model but details are very limited… once the big hyperscaler contracts have expired, they either get renewed (hopefully at higher rates) or $NBIS has to backfill that capacity with smaller deals (thankfully we don't have to worry about this for 4-5 years)… those GPUs will have been depreciated to zero (or close to it) yet they'll still have residual value making those nextgen contracts significantly more profitable… based on everything I see, hear and read… we are still compute constrained by a meaningful amount… I don’t think that ends anytime soon… not if we’re still in the early innings of ai adoption with token consumption likely growing 100-500x over the next ~5 years… I’m curious how much more upside there might be on MW rates especially on short term deals via spot/auctions… certainly possible we see spot prices hit $60M+ per MW for Vera Rubin but I’d never model those rates into my long term models… I have 9 different models for $NBIS with different inputs for GW deployed by 2031, blended MW rate and share count but generally speaking for my 2031 base case I’m using ~$20M per MW for my blended rate across 5-6GW of deployed compute and that doesn't include anything yet for the asset light business since I have no idea what the economics might look like... $NBIS is guiding to 5GW for 2030... I'm factoring in some small delays along the way but I think there's a good chance that number gets increased by 0.5-1.0GW per year which means by the time we get to 2031 I'm thinking they could be at 8+ GW plus rev share on the asset light strategy (perhaps across 2-6 GW)... will continue to adjust my models as we get more information on capacity, MW rates and the asset light model.

Add it up and my $NBIS base case models for 2031 are in the range of $100-120B revenues with 30-40% ebit margins... of course these numbers will likely be too high or too low... that's why I'll continue to adjust them as we go... my bull case models are using higher numbers for both revenues and ebit margins... in my most bullish model (unicorn) for 2031... I'm at 9GW deployed at $20M per MW with 45% ebit margins and then 3GW on the asset light model (with rev share) at 85% ebit margins... throw a reasonable multiple on that combined ebit number and the $NBIS valuation gets pretty wild. 

Of course there will be headwinds and hurdles over the next 5 years... possible delays in permits, construction and grid connects... bottlenecks in the supply chains and labor shortages... the bears will continue to spread FUD every chance they get... but I'll say this... if ai is the transformational technology that many of us believe it is... and we're still in the early innings of ai adoption... then we're also in the early innings of the ai infrastructure buildout... in which case I believe $NBIS should be a core holding.

originalText:
$QQQ Nasdaq 💻

I am NOT calling for a crash
- but we need to be aware of this distribution

📰 Last two months:
• Nvidia's guidance sparked a tech-only rally 
- $CRM+20% $CRWD $OKTA +9% earnings helped too
— but the Dow only had 6 of 30 stocks green.

• Fed's Warsh flagged sticky inflation heading into Jackson Hole, cooling rate-cut odds.

ROUNDING TOP building since April. 
QQQ has now stalled right under that same rolling dome three separate times since May.

🛎️ 702  is the support  I'm watching 

Now the breadth story, because that's what this chart is really about. 

Breadth measures how many stocks are actually participating in a move, not just what a cap-weighted index dominated by a handful of mega caps is doing. 

The McClellan Oscillator (bottom panel) is a breadth-momentum tool built off the 19-day and 39-day EMAs of NYSE advancers minus decliners. Above zero = broad participation. Below zero = fewer and fewer names carrying the tape, even while price looks fine.

⭐️ Correlation isn't causation 
(but worth watching)

Back in May, the oscillator rolled over into that "no correlation" stretch and QQQ shrugged it off, grinding higher for another month. But in mid-to-late July, that same kind of rollover came right before QQQ's sharpest drop of the summer, straight down into the high-$660s. 

Now it's rolling over a third time, right back at the top of the range — and it's not just this chart. 

The McClellan OSC has stayed negative since mid-August, new 52-week highs across the S&P have shrunk to just 1-4% of members (a healthy market runs 10-12%), and only 54% of stocks are above their 50-day moving average, down from 70% a couple weeks ago.

A third rollover at the same ceiling, with this little participation underneath a near-record print, is what DISTRIBUTION looks like. 

I'm watching 702 closely and leaning bearish here until breadth actually confirms the price.
evidenceSpan: I'm watching 702 closely and leaning bearish here until breadth actually confirms the price.
activityTitleZH: 认为QQQ在702美元附近形成圆顶分布，三次未能突破同一阻力位，且市场广度恶化（麦克莱伦振荡器转负、新高股占比下降），因此看跌QQQ，直到广度确认价格走势。

originalText:
Started writing this day after $NVDA earnings and didn't have time to finish until now:

Interesting though, not the least bit surprising, that a lot of chips and networking names are flattish today while $NVDA rallies. They have very much been inversely correlated lately.

This is why I sold 80 $FN yesterday on the afterhours earnings jump, at $438 to $454. The latter was exact top yesterday afterhours. $ANET, $COHR, $LITE, $CIEN, and so on followed similar pattern.

These are not that +50 I kept from July 29th at $404-409 but rather, the 80 I re-added back last week at $418-419.

Given the CBO on Fabrinet the last month, my net cost after factoring realized gains on the new shares is definitely close to $200, perhaps lower. Not going to bother to calculate exactly.

Given that Fabrinet is direct proxy for NVIDIA, in theory  if you believe $NVDA will do what it hopes, you would actually be buying $FN here as an overlooked and perhaps undervalued way to play it.

I on the other hand, do not question NVIDIA's guidance.

I only question the assumptions it relies on, which requires no shocks to system.

As I had to remind someone this morning, yesterday before their earnings I said $NVDA to $10T is very possible, but it assumes status quo can continue.

Every few years when we get major shocks, most people are flabbergasted and say things like it's a once in century event, so how could they prepare for such a scenario?

The problem with such simple thinking is you are looking at the risks of 1 in a 100 year (or however long) events independently, rather than the cumulative risk of just ONE happening over X period of time.

If any one = same effect on stock or market at whole, why are you only worried about the risk of one, while ignoring others?

Furthermore, many human-induced problems are erratic and first-time in history. Tech of last 100 years wasn't around for 99.999%+ of human history. Only natural events, like earthquakes and geomagnetic storms, are a not if, but when question. Human-induced are more likely ifs.

When you consider all of these together, you realize how much more precarious valuations and longer term financial assumptions are. 

You also realize that, if you want highly lucrative returns, you're not going to get there by just buying great stocks at fair prices or even at their lowest quartile of valuations.

You get there by buying shocks.

thesis: Author argues AAOI's drop on ATM offering is overdone as capital will fund capacity expansion to support 2027/2028 growth targets, implying bullish stance.
originalText:
Friday afternoon $AAOI announced a $600M ATM offering... doing this on a Friday at 5pm is definitely frowned upon however if you listened to the $AAOI fireside chat from the Rosenblatt conference last week... this offering should not be a surprise.

Personally I don't think $AAOI should be down ~12% today on ~6% dilution because this cap raise is clearly going to capex which will expand their capacity in Texas to support and possibly surpass their 2027/2028 targets.

Here is some of the Q&A commentary from the fireside chat...

Analyst asks if they're still targeting $471M per month by mid 2027... "Yeah. That's our current expectation. Based on our discussions with customers, the demand is not the limiting factor. We could actually do more revenue than that if we had more capacity at that point or sooner."

This seems pretty clear to me... $AAOI is raising more capital so they can build capacity faster and bigger to capture more of the demand coming in 2027/2028.

With regards to capex, he said... "We are going to continue to make those necessary investments. We said that the back half of the year will be at least as big as the first half of the year. All of that capex is going into production equipment and machinery, a little bit into R&D and some into real estate to support this additional production capacity"

He said the ROI for this capex is 9-10 months.

He said... "as long as we continue to see demand and we have capital available, I'll make those investments all day long."

He said the biggest risk right now is not moving fast enough or being aggressive enough with increasing capacity which means customers might go somewhere else. "If another customer came to us, and some have, and said 'we need x number of units'... We would have to say "sorry, we are sold out through second half of next year and beyond" .

Obviously no shareholder likes dilution and ATM offering announcements on a Friday afternoon is less than ideal but it's pretty clear to me this company is raising capital to continue building capacity so they can ramp revenues to $450-550M per month by mid 2027 and $550-650M per month by end of 2027 which means 2028 could be $7-9B which is 20x growth from just a couple years ago.

If you want to own a company that can grow revenues by 10-20x over 2-3 years... well then you should probably expect some dilution along the way. The best hypergrowth stories can get pretty bumpy and frustrating but these pullbacks create buying opportunities for long-term investors.

I'll gladly take 6% dilution if it means $AAOI has a better chance of hitting the numbers I mentioned above. Someday they'll have enough OCF/FCF to finance additional capex but they're not there yet.

Hopefully this is the last offering for at least 3-6 months.

I expect $META to continue to underperform the S&P 500 near-term as the outcome of a $1 trillion trial in Northern CA overhangs the stock. Like tobacco litigation 30 years ago, $META is being sued by California and a multi-state coalition of attorneys general who have argued that $META designed Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children and teens, improperly collected their data, and misled the public about the platforms' safety. The trial in federal court in Oakland before U.S. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers who was appointed by Barack Obama is likely to overhang the stock until the advisory jury renders a verdict in October.  The advisory jury is hearing the evidence and issues a verdict;  the judge is the ultimate decision-maker on liability, penalties, and remedies.  On appeal, the case would go to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, which is widely viewed as one of the more liberal circuits in the U.S. federal court system. 

In the spring, Meta (along with $GOOGL ‘s YouTube) lost a landmark social media case in California, in which a jury found the companies liable for harming a young user with certain design features in their apps and awarded her $6 million.  Then, earlier this month, $META was ordered to pay more than $940 million in the state of New Mexico for being a public nuisance and causing psychological harm to children.  In the current state AG case in Oakland the plaintiffs are asking for compensatory and punitive damages which could total $1.4 trillion, essentially equal to META’s market cap.

While $META remains cheap at 15.6x 2026 Adj EPS vs +15% long-term EPS growth, the potential for a trillion dollar initial judgment and an unfavorable appellate process before the liberal Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals could overhang the stock just like tobacco litigation impacted tobacco stocks for years until investors realized the tobacco companies could price future ligation costs into each pack of cigarettes and addicted smokers would pay it. Unlike tobacco stocks there is no pricing mechanism that $META can use to offset the risk of litigation.  $META could settle this case for a few hundred billion dollars and the stock could rise but other litigation will surely follow.

thesis: The author argues Uber's stock is undervalued as the market overreacts to robo-taxi threats, citing strong fundamentals and low valuation, and expresses a bullish view.
originalText:
$UBER Stock Looks Cheap. 
Here's Why. 

By Andrew Bary 
08/14/2026 - Barron's

Robo-taxis make up just 1% of U.S. rides. But the disruption threat of autonomous vehicles to Uber Technologies has become an obsession on Wall Street -- and has depressed the value of the company's stock. 

Investors, however, seem to be overreacting to the robo risk -- and an apparent fraying in Uber's relationship with Waymo, the leader in autonomous vehicles. The fact is that Uber remains dominant in ride-hailing, is the market leader in food delivery, and has an autonomous-vehicle strategy that doesn't rely on Alphabet's Waymo. 

Uber's stock, now trading around $76, looks appealing at nearly its lowest valuation since going public in 2019. 
"Valuation is increasingly disconnected from its fundamentals," wrote investor Bill Ackman last week in an investor letter, noting that the company's earnings are expected to rise 35% this year. Uber is one of Ackman's largest holdings. His firm, Pershing Square, owned over $2 billion of Uber on March 31. 

The stock is down 7% year to date, and up 69% since its initial public offering at $45 a share. That's way below the returns on the S&P 500 index and technology leaders like Apple, https://t.co/m3sN3qQTUX, and Alphabet. Uber now trades at about 17 times projected 2027 earnings and for about 12 times expected 2027 free cash flow of $13 billion. 

The disruption risk to Uber, which dominates the market for ride-sharing involving drivers, is far off. It's probably going to take years for robo-taxis to account for a significant share of U.S. rides. They're now in about seven cities, and will rise to 15 by year end. 

The rollout of robo-taxis has been far slower than proponents anticipated. They face technology, regulatory, and political obstacles, plus the reluctance of many Americans to trust driverless cars. 

Uber, to be sure, is positioning itself to be a major participant in the robo market even if Waymo, the leader in autonomous vehicles, moves away from its Uber partnership. But it is facing another threat in the form of Tesla and its robo-taxi strategy, which is now in the early stages. 

That all aside, there's a good case to be made for Uber. 

Why? Uber amounts to a technology utility that dominates the ride-hailing ecosystem with eight times the revenue of No. 2 Lyft. It takes a cut of the fares paid to drivers and has a growing ad business. 

Uber is valued at a discount to both the electric utility sector and S&P 500 index with faster growth. Utilities and the S&P trade for about 20 times next year's projected earnings. 

"The market sentiment and stock market valuation of Uber imply greater robo-taxi roadkill than I think is warranted," says Mark Mahaney, an analyst at Evercore ISI. 

"The market underappreciates the structural advantage of Uber as a massive demand aggregator and underestimates its ability to get robo-taxis into its fleet," he says. 

The company, Mahaney adds, has over 200 million active customers who use its services each month. He has an Outperform rating on Uber and an admittedly ambitious price target of $150 a share. 

Mahaney calls Uber a "dislocated high quality" stock, meaning it's out of favor with investors. (He puts depressed Netflix and Meta Platforms in the same category.) 

Uber's recent second-quarter earnings report highlighted its still-robust growth. Revenue was up 11%, to $14 billion, and gross bookings rose 22%, to $58 billion -- both adjusted for currency -- while adjusted earnings rose 35%, to 81 cents a share. 

The company guided to similar growth in the third quarter in bookings and adjusted earnings. 

Free cash flow totaled $10 billion over the past 12 months and is expected to hit $13 billion in 2027, resulting in an 8% free-cash-flow yield. Uber doesn't pay a dividend but aims to use half of its free cash flow for stock repurchases.

originalText:
Once, twice, maybe three times a year, you get a great opportunity to short $UVXY after a major volatility spike.

I’ve spoken extensively about $UVXY over the years, and you can read the countless tweets I’ve written explaining exactly how it works.

The basic idea is simple: $UVXY is structurally designed to lose value over time. When VIX futures are in contango, it constantly pays the roll cost, creating long-term decay. This is why it has repeatedly needed reverse splits.

The last move was from around $63 to $20, a decline of about 68%.

thesis: Author shares bullish view on TMDX after conference, highlighting margin improvements into 2026-2027 and management guidance of at least 25% operating margins by 2028 and above 30% by 2030, with growth drivers like CHOPS and OCS 2.0 contrib
originalText:
Over the last 2 days I met with 14 companies at the Canaccord Genuity conference in Boston... shoutout to @CG_Driven for putting together a really nice event. 

Some of the companies I met with were $TMDX, $IREN, $CLS, $CIFR, $SHAZ, $GLXY, $TWLO, $DDOG, $LWLG, $CLSK, $ENHA, $ZETA and several others that I need to keep private for now. 

Over the next few days I'll probably dribble out some thoughts... I'll start with $TMDX ...

$TMDX did a 10-minute presentation then a fireside chat with the CG analyst. I was sitting in the back of the room. Then the CEO & CFO did a few small group meetings, I was in one of them.

Overall the message around strategy and long-term opportunity was similar to what we've been hearing for the past few years. I'm not going to get into OCS, NOP, CHOPS, OCS 2.0, Europe expansion, etc. since most of us understand the underlying story.

MARGINS:
They're obviously compressed this year from the current investment cycle into R&D, trials and international expansion. Margins should improve slightly into 2026 2H and continue to improve into 2027 1H with the biggest margin improvements in 2027 2H. They said operating margins will be at least 25% in 2028 and could be closer to 30% with operating margins above 30% by 2030. 

CHOPS:
Should start contributing in late 2026; will be big growth driver in 2027 and beyond. 

OCS 2.0 TRIALS:
Could start contributing in late 2026 and/or early 2027; will be big growth driver in 2027 and maybe 2028.

OCS KIDNEY:
Should start contributing in 2027 2H; will be big growth driver in 2028 and beyond.

ORGAN UTILIZATION:
This is where big improvements can be made especially if $TMDX becomes an OPO, should know later this year.

It costs CMS approx $10.5B per year to keep 100,000+ people on the organ donor list. With better organ utilization (using OCS/NOP) plus OCS Kidney (when its available)... $TMDX could save CMS at least $1-2B per year which obviously justifies their service/prices not to mention the lives they are saving. 

DRY RUNS:
Management continues to say that dry runs have not increased and I believe them. They're doing more internal flights on $TMDX owned planes versus external/charter flights, perhaps this is where the confusion came from. Over the past 6-12 months they've gone from 75-80% internal flights to 85-90% internal flights... doing more double shifts have allowed this to happen... this increase in internal flights should be better for margins going forward as it increases utilization on company owned planes. 

REVENUE TARGETS:
They said revenues will be at least $2B in 2032 but could be higher... when I asked about $3B since this is the number they floated at the William Blair conference 2 months ago... they chuckled and said "well, that is higher than $2B so it's possible" 

REVENUE GROWTH:
By far this was the most important thing I heard from $TMDX this week... they confirmed what I already thought needed to happen in order to hit their 2030 targets for OCS cases (which is currently 10,000 and does not include CHOPS)... $TMDX management is saying that revenue growth will accelerate in 2027, 2028 and 2029.

They didn't give any specific acceleration targets, however if we assume revenue growth comes in at 25% in 2026 (high end of current guidance) and accelerates by 250 bps per year for each of the next 3 years...(fueled by OCS 1.0, CHOPS, OCS 2.0 Trials, OCS Kidney and European expansion)... this puts 2029 revenues at approx $1.665B

Management is saying 2028 operating margins will be 25-30%, let's use the midpoint at 27.5% for 2028 and then assume they get to 30% in 2029 which should put income margins in 2029 at 20% or higher. 

$1.665B revenues in 2029 with 20% net income margins is approx $333M of net income.

This year, because of compressed margins from the ongoing investment cycle, net income is expected to be $60M, down from $106M in 2025.

Going from $60M of net income in 2026 to $333M of net income in 2029 is a 3-year net income CAGR of 77%

Right now the stock is trading at a multiple which is a fraction of that potential growth rate over the next 3+ years.

Of course I've been frustrated with $TMDX over the past 6+ months... I think management could have done a better job communicating with shareholders and analysts.. I think $TMDX needs to bring in a medtech veteran to bolster the c-suite... however... the long term thesis still looks very compelling especially at the current valuation in the middle of an investment cycle which is being done to accelerate growth over the next 3-5 years.

Right now you can by $TMDX at 3.5x 2027 revenues while the CEO/CFO are telling you that revenue growth is going to accelerate in 2027, 2028 and 2029. 

This has the potential to be one of the best non-ai growth stories over the next few years with revenue growth accelerating while net income margins go from 8% in 2026 to 20% or higher in 2029. 

That combination of revenue growth acceleration plus margin expansion should/could re-rate the ev/revs multiple from 3-4x up to 6-8x. 

If you put an 8x exit multiple on 2029 revenues and assume minimal dilution over next 4 years then you get to a $350+ stock price going into 2030 which is 300% higher than current prices. 

FWIW, $ISRG is trading at 11x NTM revenues with growth decelerating from 20% in 2025, to 17% in 2026 to 12% in 2027 (using sell side estimates)... whereas $TMDX will be accelerating growth from 25% in 2026 to 30-35% in 2029... much different backdrop and one that will justify multiple expansion from here.

thesis: Author, with deep knowledge of ZIM, believes the buyout story is over and sold ~$33k of puts expiring next week at ~$24.70, while citing rising freight rates as a bullish driver.
originalText:
Easy Money

Everybody laughed at Mark Minervini when he got caught on CNBC talking about a company he clearly didn’t know very well. But let’s be honest: 99% of people on X are exactly the same.

Most people here can talk confidently about 100 stocks. Ask them to go really deep and they probably know two of them well, if they’re lucky.

And I’m no different. When someone asks me about a random company, most of the time I simply say, “I don’t know.” Because I really don’t know anything of real value about 99% of the companies in the stock market.

That’s the point.

If you’ve been following me on $ZIM, you already know I believe the buyout story ended a long time ago. The government rejected it, the prime minister rejected it, and I expect the formal announcement very soon. Most smart investors already figured this out, and Israeli institutional investors have started buying again.

But apparently some algos, foreign investors, and a few people here on X who think they understand what is happening in Israel still believe there is a 5%, 10% or 20% chance the deal happens. I think the odds are closer to 0.1%.

So every time another newspaper article comes out saying the buyout isn’t going to happen, $ZIM gets hit again.

This time it fell to around $24.70. I immediately said I was happy to sell more puts there, and I sold around $33,000 worth of puts expiring next week(see below).

I didn’t need to start researching. I didn’t need to read 20 articles. I didn’t need to build another model. I already know the situation.

At the same time, anyone following shipping can see freight rates keep climbing and companies across the industry continue making serious money. $ZIM should be one of the biggest beneficiaries because its earnings are more sensitive to spot rates.

That is the advantage of knowing a few situations extremely well.

And this is probably exactly how the two hedge funds that helped found $WGS felt when everyone panicked and crashed the stock to around $35. They had a superior understanding of the company and the situation, so while everyone else was panicking, they could immediately put more than $150 million into the stock. A few months later, the stock had more than doubled.

For them, it probably didn’t even feel like a big bet. They knew the company better than almost anyone else in the market. From their point of view, it was taking candy from a child.

You can know 5% about 100 stocks and always have something to say.

Or you can know a few companies so well that when the market gives you a stupid price, you don’t need a week to figure out what to do. You can act in one minute.

thesis: The author believes IREN's strategy of delaying discounted compute sales allows for higher pricing at launch, signaling strong long-term potential, making it a bullish call.
originalText:
$NBIS $IREN $CRWV It blows me mind as a Nebius and IREN shareholder that people would sell these two names to buy CoreWeave. 

Tell me you don't understand the sector, without actually telling it.😉

The most common phrase here is that CoreWeave is so cheap here. They have so much more revenue and revenue backlog then Nebius and IREN. Well unfortunately that's the sector novice take.

Side step story 
$RKLB CEO Sir Peter Beck is famous for not building a revenue backlog for its Neutron rocket years early even though it could have massively supported the stock price when it was a fraction of what it is today. Competitor Relativity Space was famous for sporting a massive backlog in the billions of dollar by offering heavily discounted launches.
 
He knew that from building his Electron rocket that if you sell launch slots years in advance you have to heavily discount them and it took Rocket Lab years to flush these cheap launch slots out of the manifest. Instead of optimizing for revenue backlog he optimized for revenue. 

Fastforward till today, Neutron rocket is close to launch and each quarter new launch slots are booked at the full price. Relativity Space almost went under until it was bought by Eric Schmidt who kicked out the prior management team.

Moral of the story: You want to invest in management teams that optimize the business, not just the stock!

IREN's revenue backlog is way more limited, because instead of offering heavily discounted compute deals a long time in advance they are waiting until sites are powered and the most important deliverables are installed. The shorter the time to compute, the higher price you can ask from your customers. In addition even though they had a massive gap IREN is currently making the right moves with Mirantis to move into enterprise a la Nebius and don't make the same mistake CoreWeave made optimizing on low value revenue and backlog.

Nebius follows a similar playbook where each deal was highly strategic. Microsoft for the at the time industry leading 40% prepayment and Meta for the 15 billion backstop that allows them to finance that amount and then sell it to enterprise. Nebius management team went on record is that they hate these deals, but that they needed just a few to finance the build out the enterprise business and they also said they will do only one more of such deal before stopping it indefinitely.

CoreWeave management team, besides being the remnants of a failed Ethereum miner, pulled a complete Relativity Space playbook:
> Sign low value high volume hyperscaler deals up to 100 billion that optimize revenue and backlog
> Don't own any of the underlying infrastructure
> Massive debt
> Massive insider selling from management

So here we have a management team selling discounted low margin high volume hyperscaler deals years in advance on infrastructure they rent and don't own together with massive debt and insider selling from management? Their main goal is to make the stock look good instead of the business.

You need to invest in management teams that mainly optimize the business instead of just the stock.

In 5 years IREN and Nebius have a massively paid of portfolio of AI datacenter infrastructure that they can sell on short notice to the highest bidder, while CoreWeave has idle GPU's collecting dust if they don't pay 2-3x the rent of what they are paying in 2026. The lesson here is just because CoreWeave pulled everything forward to make the stock look good does not make the business cheap. In fact I will go on record here CoreWeave is the most expensive stock of all three Neoclouds, because a) management team that has the wrong strategy and that results in them not holding any AI infrastructure. Recommend to stay far away!
evidenceSpan: IREN's revenue backlog is way more limited, because instead of offering heavily discounted compute deals a long time in advance they are waiting until sites are powered and the most important deliverables are installed. The shorter the time to compute, the higher price you can ask from your customers.
activityTitleZH: 认为IREN因不提前低价出售算力而能以更高价格定价，具备长期增长潜力，属于看涨观点。
activityTitleEN: Believes IREN's strategy of delaying discounted compute sales allows for higher pricing at launch, signaling strong long-term potential, making it a bullish call.

从风险收益比来看，此前止损设于189，目标为214，现目标已提升至236，整体回报率极具吸引力。若最终抵达终极高点，可考虑在236完成全部平仓。214是Nvidia最重要的技术转折点，一旦失守，可能意味着假突破或波动性驱动的“牛市陷阱”，随后可能回撤至21日均线甚至200区间。因此，该价位是必须紧盯的核心支撑。

自6月20日首次买入信号以来，我们多次在214附近进行买卖操作，验证了该位置的长期有效性。通过严格执行风险管理与交易策略，可有效消除交易中的四大恐惧：亏损恐惧、错失良机恐惧、落袋为安恐惧、犯错恐惧。当前策略正是通过部分止盈与保留头寸，实现风险控制与机会捕捉的平衡。

特斯拉当前下跌1.77%，但已反弹至297附近支撑位，该位置为此前买入点。目标价仍为342，若1小时图显示回测21小时均线，则为正常回调。若跌破今日低点及21小时均线，可能引发更深调整，目标或下探至297。不过目前仍处于健康运行状态，未见明确反转信号。

AMD今日下跌7%，收复前期缺口，形成顶部信号。若能进一步回落，接近支撑区则更具投资价值。理想情况下，应在支撑位附近出现看涨反应，以获取更优的风险收益比。但当前尚未出现此类信号，且未靠近支撑区，因此暂不构成买入条件。建议观望，等待更清晰的入场机会。

Palantir近期在报告后形成顶部信号，位于关键阻力区下方。该位置为长期形成的双阻力位，此前多次作为交易目标。我们曾多次在此区域买卖，表明其重要性。若未能在支撑区企稳，可能继续回调至136或21日均线，甚至完全回补缺口。因此，当前不宜买入，但若认为过热，可在阻力区选择卖出，合理设置止损与目标，才是专业交易者应有的做法。

Irene（IREN）今日收出看跌蜡烛，收盘低于当日低点，若明日确认跌破21日均线，将强化回调信号，目标位为30至32美元之间的双重支撑区。若能回升并突破21小时均线，创出新高，则可避免熊市情景。当前处于敏感阶段，需密切关注下一波突破方向。若向上突破42美元，则可能开启新一轮上涨，目标或上探60美元。

SanDisk在财报后盘后大跌，再次形成顶部信号，且面临21日均线的强阻力。当前价格已开始回补缺口，1小时图显示接近短期支撑位。若继续下行，跌破支撑，将确认熊市延续，目标位为998（约1000美元整数关口）。目前仍处于低于21日均线、低点不断降低的状态，缺乏反弹迹象，因此不建议介入，待更明确的企稳信号出现后再考虑。
